security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates a Zilsd 64-bit load/store (LD/SD/C.LD/C.SD/C.LDSP/C.SDSP) on RV32 as two independent 32-bit memory accesses without enforcing atomicity of the combined 64-bit transfer, OR fails to validate that the register-pair operand (rd/rs2) is even-numbered per the [[norm:Zilsd_reg_pairs]] rule, OR exposes stale data in the upper half of the destination register pair when a trap occurs mid-execution of a split 64-bit load.
security_spec.summary: Zilsd 64-bit loads/stores on RV32 use aligned even/odd register pairs; QEMU must atomically perform the combined 64-bit memory transfer in TCG, validate register-pair alignment at translate time, and ensure no stale upper-half register state is observable on mid-instruction traps — failure risks torn reads/writes under multi-hart SMP and guest-visible data corruption.

findings.finding: Missing decode_save_opc(ctx, 0) before tcg_gen_qemu_ld_i64(). Every other load/store translation helper in QEMU (gen_load at trans_rvi.c.inc:416, trans_fld at trans_rvd.c.inc:65, gen_store at trans_rvi.c.inc:527, trans_fsd at trans_rvd.c.inc:90, AMOCAS at trans_rvzacas.c.inc:80) calls decode_save_opc() before memory ops to set env->bins. Without it, riscv_transformed_insn() at cpu_helper.c:2282 uses stale env->bins, corrupting mtinst/htinst on all load faults.
findings.snippet:
tcg_gen_qemu_ld_i64(tmp, addr, ctx->mem_idx, MO_SQ | mo_endian(ctx));
    // NOTE: decode_save_opc(ctx, 0) is MISSING here

findings.finding: Missing decode_save_opc(ctx, 0) before tcg_gen_qemu_st_i64(). Same root cause as gen_load_i64 — stale env->bins breaks tinst reconstruction on store faults (page faults, access faults, misaligned).
findings.snippet:
tcg_gen_qemu_st_i64(tmp, addr, ctx->mem_idx, MO_SQ | mo_endian(ctx));
    // NOTE: decode_save_opc(ctx, 0) is MISSING here

findings.finding: tcg_gen_qemu_ld_i64() uses bare MO_SQ | mo_endian(ctx) with no atomicity qualifier. The Zilsd spec v1.0 Section 2.1 requires naturally-aligned 64-bit LD/SD on RV32 to be atomic. Compare trans_fld at trans_rvd.c.inc:56-62 which checks get_xl_max(ctx)==RV32→MO_ATOM_NONE, zama16b→MO_ATOM_WITHIN16, else→MO_ATOM_IFALIGN. On 64-bit hosts TCG emits a single insn (masked), but on 32-bit hosts/TCI a naturally-aligned 64-bit access can tear into two 32-bit halves, violating the ISA atomicity guarantee.

tcg_gen_qemu_st_i64() uses bare MO_SQ | mo_endian(ctx) with no atomicity qualifier. Same atomicity violation as gen_load_i64 at line 33. Naturally-aligned 64-bit stores to device MMIO or shared memory can tear on 32-bit hosts, causing data corruption visible to other harts/devices.

Early return at line 35-37 when rd==0 skips the dest pair write to x0 (valid since x0 is hardwired zero), but the tcg_gen_qemu_ld_i64 at line 33 still executes and can fault. With the missing decode_save_opc, the fault handler sees stale env->bins. However even with decode_save_opc added, the early return discards the loaded value but does not discard the fault — this is actually spec-compliant (loads to x0 must still check permissions and can fault), but the interaction with the missing decode_save_opc makes fault attribution doubly broken.

On RV32 with Zclsd, C.LD (Quadrant 0, funct3=011, OPC_RISC_C_FUNC_FLW_LD) enters the C.FLW path because riscv_cpu_xlen(env)==32. This reconstructs tinst as OPC_RISC_FLW (float load word) with C.LW-format immediate (GET_C_LW_IMM) and access_size=4, but Zclsd C.LD uses the @cl_d format with different immediate bit layout, access_size=8, and should reconstruct as OPC_RISC_LD. The tinst CSR delivered to the OS trap handler is semantically wrong.

On RV32 with Zclsd, C.SD (Quadrant 0, funct3=111, OPC_RISC_C_FUNC_FSW_SD) enters the C.FSW path with OPC_RISC_FSW, C.SW-format immediate, access_size=4. Zclsd C.SD uses @cs_d format, access_size=8, and should reconstruct as OPC_RISC_SD. Same category as C.LD — wrong tinst reconstruction.

On RV32 with Zclsd, C.LDSP (Quadrant 2, funct3=011, OPC_RISC_C_FUNC_FLWSP_LDSP) enters the C.FLWSP path with OPC_RISC_FLW, C.LWSP-format immediate, access_size=4. Zclsd C.LDSP uses @c_ldsp format with different immediate layout, access_size=8, and should reconstruct as OPC_RISC_LD.

On RV32 with Zclsd, C.SDSP (Quadrant 2, funct3=111/7) enters the C.FSWSP path with OPC_RISC_FSW, C.SWSP-format immediate, access_size=4. Zclsd C.SDSP uses @c_sdsp format, access_size=8, and should reconstruct as OPC_RISC_SD.

Even-register validation for rd correctly checks if (a->rd) % 2 and returns false (triggering illegal instruction). This enforces the Zilsd [[norm:Zilsd_reg_pairs]] rule that the destination register in the pair must be even-numbered.
Even-register validation for rs2 correctly checks if (a->rs2) % 2 and returns false. This enforces the Zilsd [[norm:Zilsd_reg_pairs]] rule for the source register pair in stores.

REQUIRE_32BIT(ctx) correctly restricts translation to RV32-only (get_xl(ctx) != MXL_RV32 → returns false). On RV64/RV128, the existing RV64I LD/SD instructions take precedence in the decode overlap. This is spec-compliant — Zilsd is an RV32-only extension.

Implied extension rules are correctly implemented: Zilsd+RVC → Zclsd (line 1130-1132), and Zclsd → Zca+Zilsd (line 1134-1137). This ensures the compressed sub-extension is properly auto-enabled when the compressed ISA is present.
trans_zclsd_ldsp correctly rejects rd==0 (returns false/illegal instruction), matching the RISC-V C extension rule that C.LDSP with rd=x0 is reserved.

gen_store_i64 correctly handles rs2==0 by using tcg_constant_i64(0) instead of the concat path. Since x0 is hardwired to zero, a store from register pair (x0, x1) would store (0, x1). The special-casing of rs2==0 treats it as a 64-bit store of all zeros, which is correct per ISA semantics (the lower register in the pair is x0=0).

Zilsd LD and SD are correctly defined as decode-overloads of the RV64I LD/SD opcode space (LOAD opcode 0000011 funct3=011, STORE opcode 0100011 funct3=011) inside { } blocks. On RV32 with Zilsd, the decoder selects zilsd_ld/zilsd_sd via REQUIRE_32BIT in the trans function. On RV64, the standard ld/sd variants take precedence since zilsd trans functions return false via REQUIRE_32BIT.

The trap handler's tval assignment path for LOAD/STORE exceptions (line 2260-2270: sets tval=env->badaddr, calls riscv_transformed_insn for tinst) would function correctly IF decode_save_opc were called in the Zilsd trans functions. The infrastructure is correct — the bug is solely in the trans functions not populating env->bins.
